newsitem.title: UK: Crude lifts Med oil products,but local buys limited.
newsitem.headline: Crude lifts Med oil products,but local buys limited.

text.p: Mediterranean oil product markets were stronger on Monday as crude's strength raised prices across the board, traders said.
Gas oil firmed on the back of stronger futures and good buying interest to fill recent East Med tenders.
Premiums to benchmark quotes for Russian 0.2 pct cargoes held firm near high fob quotes +$1.50 a tonne while Italian barrels were looking for high fob quotes +$2-3 a tonne.
Gas oil supplies were expected to build despite tighter Russian avails with the end of Med refinery turnarounds increasing output and the closing of the arb to Asia.
Premiums for well supplied EN590 remained soft at fob high EN590 quotes +$2.
Gasoline was firm in a tightish, well-bid market.
An Italian refiner was looking for a 95 ron premium unleaded cargo, Turkey had tendered for 20-25,000 tonnes of 90 ron leaded and Slovenia sought 25-27,000 tonnes via a French refiner.
Cargo prices for premium unleaded material were assessed around $215/$217 cif Med. Some players noted that a dearth of suitable gasoline vessels was also bumping up prices.
Naphtha was steady as surging crude prices counterbalanced the effects of stilted buying interest.
Fuel oil markets were inactive, with traders preferring to sit back and assess the strength of crude's rally.
Straight-run cargoes from Russia were asking higher premia on the back of crude's rally but interest was limited to two slow-moving Italian refineries, traders said.

They predicted better interest in a few days for Russian material, though most of the bunker outlets that could take it were satisfied last week. Only a requirement in Las Palmas was needing filled, traders said
High sulphur cargoes were still being prepared for transit to the East, with the arbitrage technically profitable.
